findings.claim: The fixture-path input validation accepts relative traversal paths (../) and absolute paths. The Python guard only rejects empty strings and the three control characters \n, \r, \x00. The downstream bash existence check passes for any existing path including parent-directory escapes. The fallback `find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f` would enumerate files outside the repository root.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 190-199: Python check: `sys.exit(0 if value and all(ch not in value for ch in ('\n','\r','\x00')) else 1)`. policy-check.yml lines 201-203: bash existence check `[ ! -e "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" ]` — passes for `../`, `/tmp`, etc. policy-check.yml line 213: `find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort > changed-files.txt`. In the selftest, paths are hardcoded and non-attacker-controlled; risk is for downstream callers of the reusable workflow.
findings.impact: A misconfigured or compromised calling workflow with fixture-path: ../.. would scope OPA evaluation to the repo root's parent, potentially evaluating files outside the repository. Defense-in-depth gap; not directly exploitable in the selftest context.
findings.mitigation: Add path validation in collect-changed-files: reject (a) paths starting with / (absolute), (b) paths containing ../. Optionally: verify realpath resolves inside git rev-parse --show-toplevel. Python: `import os; root=os.path.realpath(subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','--show-toplevel'],text=True).strip()); assert resolved.startswith(root+os.sep) or resolved==root`.

findings.claim: The ratchet check in validate-selftest-config uses `git diff --name-only base..head` without a path-scope argument, producing the full PR diff. The same `changed` list is used for both the ratchet check and the SHA-pin check (string-matching against '.github/workflows/policy-check.yml'). A false-positive or false-negative on that string match would either spuriously trigger or silently miss the pin-update requirement.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 49-57: `changed = subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',f'{base}..{head}'],text=True).splitlines()`. Line 54: `if '.github/workflows/policy-check.yml' in changed`. No path-scoped invocation for the pin check. The inverse risk: if git diff ever elides .github/workflows/policy-check.yml from output, a genuine policy-check.yml change would pass the SHA check with stale pins.
findings.impact: Low probability. fetch-depth: 0 in the workflow mitigates shallow-clone elision. Primary concern is defense-in-depth precision; no direct bypass demonstrated.
findings.mitigation: Scope the pin-check diff separately: `subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',f'{base}..{head}','--','.github/workflows/policy-check.yml'],text=True).strip()` and check if non-empty. Keep the full diff for the ratchet check which genuinely needs all fixture paths.

findings.claim: fixture-pass/services.yml uses jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json. If SCP-R-001 (020C) validates jwks_url domain beyond URI-format-only (e.g., must match *.brokapps.ai or a known allowlist), example.com will produce a deny finding on the fixture-pass fixture, breaking the selftest permanently after 020C merge.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-pass/services.yml line 16: `jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. The plan §4 020C SCP-R-001 spec does not enumerate jwks_url domain-validation scope. No note in conftest.md. Unresolved since R1.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 validates jwks_url domain, fixture-pass permanently fails after 020C, blocking all downstream slices. Forward-commitment risk that must be resolved before 020C dispatch opens.
findings.mitigation: Before 020C opens: document in the SCP-R-001 rule spec whether jwks_url is format-only or domain-validated. If domain-validated, replace example.com with a value that will satisfy the rule (e.g., a valid brokapps.ai JWKS endpoint). Add a note to conftest.md.

findings.mitigation: Eliminate the ceremony by adding an artifact-name-suffix input to policy-check.yml so each invocation uploads to a distinct name directly (e.g., policy-check-summary-pass and policy-check-summary-fail). Deferred to a later slice if not blocking 020C.

findings.claim: The waivers-path input (policy-check.yml line 30: `waivers-path: string, default: output/findings/waivers.json`) has no path traversal validation. An adversary controlling the calling workflow can pass waivers-path: ../../some/valid/schema-conformant.json to cause the bypass gate to validate an unexpected file on the runner filesystem as the waiver document. Parallel gap to R2-SBP-MIN-01 (fixture-path), not previously flagged.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 64: `SCP_WAIVERS_PATH: ${{ inputs.waivers-path }}`. policy-check.yml lines 304-307: `if [ ! -f "${SCP_WAIVERS_PATH}" ]` — bash existence check with no traversal guard. policy-check.yml line 317: `waivers_path = Path(os.environ['SCP_WAIVERS_PATH'])` — Python file read with no realpath containment check. No equivalent of the Python control-character guard (policy-check.yml lines 190-199) exists for SCP_WAIVERS_PATH. The R2-SBP-MIN-01 finding explicitly covered fixture-path; waivers-path received no corresponding treatment.
findings.impact: Exploitability is lower than R2-SBP-MIN-01: (1) the bypass gate only activates when inputs.scp_bypass == true; (2) the Python schema validator at lines 317-333 fails closed on non-JSON content and on JSON that does not conform to schemas/waivers-file.schema.json; (3) post-020K, caller workflow files are CODEOWNER-gated. Primary residual risk: a misconfigured caller could inadvertently point waivers-path at a valid-schema-conformant JSON file outside the repository tree, silently validating it as a legitimate waiver document. Information disclosure from arbitrary readable JSON files on the runner filesystem is a secondary risk.
findings.mitigation: Add the same traversal guard as recommended for fixture-path: reject waivers-path values that (a) start with / (absolute), (b) contain the substring ../, or (c) resolve via realpath to a location outside git rev-parse --show-toplevel. Apply the guard immediately before the `[ ! -f ... ]` existence check in the bypass-gate step. This closes the symmetry gap with R2-SBP-MIN-01.
